content.title: Final Four results: Michigan, UConn advance to men's national championship
content.text: 11d ago / 11:47 PM EDTDusty May on UConn matchup: Michigan 'will be up for the challenge' During the first national semifinal between Illinois and UConn, Michigan coach Dusty May sat in the crowd, scouting the Huskies, in case the two teams would later face each other in the national championship game. Well, that's exactly the matchup we'll get Monday night. Michigan vs. UConn for the title. After Michigan dismantled Arizona in the second national semifinal Saturday, TBS' Tracy Wolfson asked May about UConn. "They have championship DNA," May said. "What they've done over the last four years is as impressive as anything we've seen in recent memory. We've got our hands full Monday, but these guys will be up for the challenge."11d ago / 11:39 PM EDTYaxel Lendeborg on injury: 'There’s no way I’m missing [the] game on Monday night'After the game, Michigan star forward Yaxel Lendeborg told TBS' Tracy Wolfson that he would play in Monday's national title game against UConn, despite suffering a knee and ankle injury of tonight's game."I'm going to push through," Lendeborg said. "There's no way I'm missing [the] game on Monday night no matter what goes on. I'm going to play unless I can't walk -- at all."11d ago / 11:35 PM EDTFinal: Michigan 91, Arizona 73Our national championship game is set!Michigan will take on UConn on Monday night after a dominant showing against Arizona. The Wolverines certainly look like the team to beat after this performance. 11d ago / 11:29 PM EDTWhat will be Lendeborg's status for national title game?With this game seemingly wrapped up, the question now becomes, what will be Yaxel Lendeborg's status for Monday's national title game? Lendeborg, Michigan's leading scorer, injured his knee and ankle in the first half tonight.He returned to the game in the second half, but was moving gingerly and did not appear to be his usual, athletic self.Nevertheless, Lendeborg made two 3-pointers in the second half, a potentially encouraging sign. He scored 11 points in 14 minutes tonight.11d ago / 11:25 PM EDTMichigan 88, Arizona 66 with 3:02 to goAday Mara has dominated tonight, scoring 26 points on 11-of-16 shooting. 11d ago / 11:25 PM EDTMichigan's center Aday Mara has had a monster gameMichigan's tallest player, its 7-foot-3 center Aday Mara has been a force in the paint tonight. He's up to 26 points now, a new season-high, and has also grabbed 8 rebounds, while blocking two shots. Mara's previous season-high for points came in February, when he scored 24 against Ohio State.11d ago / 11:12 PM EDTMichigan 81, Arizona 60 at the under-8 timeoutThe Wolverines are 7:33 away from joining UConn in the national championship game. 11d ago / 11:12 PM EDTArizona on pace to allow a season-high in pointsThe most points allowed this season by an Arizona opponent is 88, by Arkansas in the Sweet 16. Arkansas is one of just seven teams to crack the 80-point barrier against the Wildcats. Michigan has 81 points — with more than eight minutes still to play. 11d ago / 11:06 PM EDTMichigan has blown out good teams all seasonEntering this game, everyone expected a tight contest between Michigan and Arizona. But the Wolverines have blown out good teams all season. In November, they beat then-No. 21 Auburn by 30 points, and then-No. 12 Gonzaga by 40 points. In January, they beat then-No. 24 USC by 30.Just last week, in the Elite Eight, Michigan beat Tennessee by 33 points. Perhaps a blowout shouldn't have been so surprising. 11d ago / 10:58 PM EDTUnsung hero for Michigan: freshman Trey McKenneyThe Wolverines built their roster with lots of transfers from other schools. Yaxel Lendeborg arrived from UAB, Aday Mara from UCLA, Elliot Cadeau from North Carolina, and Morez Johnson Jr. from Illinois.Freshman Trey McKenney is one of the rare homegrown players on the roster. He was a four-star recruit from Flint, Michigan. Tonight, he's provided a big spark off the bench, scoring 13 points so far, while making 3-of-5 attempts from 3-point range.11d ago / 10:58 PM EDTThis one looks overThe Wolverines have outscored the Wildcats 27-13 in the second half. Michigan’s lead is up to 72-45 with 12:17 left. 11d ago / 10:50 PM EDTMichigan 56, Arizona 39 at the under-16 timeoutThe Wildcats have scored the last 5 points, but they still have plenty of ground to make up with 15:40 left in regulation. 11d ago / 10:47 PM EDTStunning to see Arizona being blown out like thisYou can't say Arizona wasn't battle-tested before tonight. They are the only team in NCAA history to have 12 wins over top-25-ranked teams entering the NCAA tournament. They added two more in the NCAA tournament to bring their total to 14, the most since the AP poll began in 1949-50, according to the school.The Wildcats have played good teams all season long and are no strangers to top competition. But Michigan, leading by 19, is making Arizona look like it's not ready for this stage.11d ago / 10:47 PM EDTNot the start Arizona wanted to the second halfMichigan opened the second period on an 8-2 run and its lead ballooned to 22.An and-1 from Koa Peat cut the deficit to 19, but the Wildcats aren’t making up any ground here. 11d ago / 10:47 PM EDTLendeborg has an MCL sprain, ankle injury, but he's trying to play in the second halfOn the TBS broadcast, Tracy Wolfson reported that she spoke to Michigan's training staff, who relayed that Yaxel Lendeborg, the team's leading scorer, had suffered an MCL sprain to his left knee and an ankle injury in the first half.The training staff gave Lendeborg ice and a massage, and he's on the court now, trying to play through the pain. We'll see how effective he is the rest of the game. He has made two 3-pointers early in the second half.11d ago / 10:41 PM EDTThe second half is underwayArizona needs to get to work quickly here. 11d ago / 10:24 PM EDTCadeau on Lendeborg's potential absence: 'We still got a really good team.'At halftime, TBS interviewed Michigan point guard Elliot Cadeau and asked what the Wolverines would do if Yaxel Ladenborg is unable to return to the game, after suffering an apparent ankle injury. "We've got nine starters or our team," Cadeau said, referring to Michigan's depth. "If we don't [have him], we still got a really good team."11d ago / 10:21 PM EDTHalftime: Michigan 48, Arizona 32Outside of one Arizona run, it was all Michigan in the first half.The Wolverines lead by 16 despite shooting only 41% from field, including 31% from deep.The Wildcats will have to make their biggest comeback of the season if they want to win. Arizona hadn’t trailed by more than 7 points in any game this season before tonight. 11d ago / 10:20 PM EDTCadeau, Mara and Johnson powering Michigan in Lendeborg's absenceYaxel Lendeborg may have missed much of the first half due to foul trouble and then an injury. But the Wolverines have built a big lead thanks to their point guard, Elliot Cadeau, who's scored 5 points and dished out 6 assists, keeping the offense humming and everyone involved. Cadeau's only weak point? He's shot 2-for-14 from the field.Lendeborg's frontcourt mates, Aday Mara and Morez Johnson Jr., have also picked up the slack. Mara has scored 15 points and grabbed 5 rebounds, and Johnson has scored 8 points while grabbing 4 boards. 11d ago / 10:17 PM EDTArizona's style of play may need to changeThe Wildcats proudly buck the trend of shooting more and more 3-pointers that has taken over basketball at all levels during the past decade. Coach Tommy Lloyd has built their offense around putting pressure on defenses via drives. They have 25 games this season with 15 or fewer 3-point attempts, the most in the country.But facing a 47-30 deficit late in the first half, the Wildcats are not going to get back into this game solely on 2-point shots alone. They may need to change their long-held style.11d ago / 10:11 PM EDTMichigan 38, Arizona 25 at the under-4 timeoutThe Wolverines have taken back control of this game. They lead by 13 despite some foul and injury trouble.All five of Michigan’s starters have scored at least 5 points, led by Aday Mara’s 8. 11d ago / 10:10 PM EDTMichigan's Lendeborg's status still unclearWith less than five minutes remaining in the first half, TBS cameras caught Yaxel Lendeborg walking back to the locker room (again), with a towel over his head, after briefly emerging from the locker room. Midway through the first half, Lendeborg appeared to injure his left ankle driving to the basket. Then he walked gingerly to the locker room to receive treatment. It's unclear why Lendeborg emerged from the locker room, only to return to the locker room shortly after.According to the TBS broadcast, Lendeborg injured the same ankle during the Big Ten conference tournament. After receiving treatment, Lendeborg and the team will determine whether he can return in the second half. 11d ago / 10:06 PM EDTFoul trouble for star Arizona guardJaden Bradley has three fouls after picking up his latest for using his off-arm to create space on a drive. Bradley has earned third-team All-American honors this season from three different organizations and is averaging 13.3 points per game.11d ago / 10:05 PM EDTMichigan’s lead back up to 12After the Arizona run cut into their lead, the Wolverines have scored 7 straight points to take a 35-23 advantage with 4:35 left in the first half.11d ago / 10:03 PM EDTMichigan's frontcourt racking up foulsAll three of the Wolverines' frontcourt starters -- Yaxel Lendeborg, Morez Johnson Jr. and Aday Mara -- already have two fouls apiece.But the pressing issue is the health of Lendeborg, who just walked gingerly back to the Michigan bench, with a towel draped over his head. A few minutes ago, Lendeborg appeared to injure his ankle driving to the hoop.11d ago / 9:57 PM EDTWill Arizona's free-throw edge materialize?The Wildcats have a knack for getting to the free-throw line the likes of which haven't been seen in years. They entered tonight having attempted 1,020 free throws on the season, the most by a school in a single season since BYU (1,055) in 2013-14. You probably won't be surprised to hear, then, that Arizona leads the NCAA tournament with 88 fouls drawn, 11 more than the next-best team. 11d ago / 9:53 PM EDTWildcats fighting backAfter facing its biggest deficit of the season, Arizona is in the midst of a 11-2 run to cut the score to 28-21 with 7:21 left in the first half. 11d ago / 9:52 PM EDTMichigan's Lendeborg injures left ankleMidway through the first half, Michigan's leading scorer Yaxel Lendeborg injured his left ankle on a drive to the basket, and is now heading to the locker room. He's walking with a visible limp.According to the TBS broadcast, Lendeborg is going to ice his ankle and get it taped, and the team's staff is also examining his knee.Lendeborg picked up two fouls within the first 90 seconds of the game, and that forced him to the bench. When he finally returned to the court, he made a 3-pointer. But shortly after, he injured his ankle on that drive.11d ago / 9:49 PM EDTArizona faced largest deficit of seasonTrailing 24-10, and then 26-10, Arizona found itself trailing by its largest amount of the entire season here midway through the first half of this national semifinal. 11d ago / 9:43 PM EDTArizona's perimeter defense getting testedMichigan is 3-for-7 on 3-pointers so far, and I'm going to watch if this can continue, because Arizona has made life very difficult for opponents from deep.In this NCAA tournament, Arizona has held opponents to 27.9% 3-point shooting. Is Michigan's shooting the exception, or will it regress to the mean? 11d ago / 9:41 PM EDTMichigan 22, Arizona 10 at the under-12 timeoutThe Wolverines’ Aday Mara leads all scorers with 6 points. Michigan is shooting 50% from the field compared to 33% for the Wildcats. 11d ago / 9:39 PM EDTWatch: big-time block by Arizona's Koa PeatPeat is an electric athlete, in a game full of them. 11d ago / 9:36 PM EDTMichigan sharing the ball well early onThe Wolverines have five assists on seven made baskets already, and they're being led by point guard Elliot Cadeau, a transfer from North Carolina. He has three assists so far, and has been averaging 8.3 assists per game in the NCAA Tournament. Morez Johnson Jr. also just made an nifty pass to fellow big man Aday Mara for an easy bucket. 11d ago / 9:35 PM EDTMichigan’s lead now double digitsThe Wolverines continue to cruise early. A Trey McKinney dunk has Michigan up 16-5, forcing an Arizona timeout.The Wildcats have 14:27 left in the first to start clawing back.11d ago / 9:33 PM EDTArizona unbeaten vs. top-10 teams this seasonOn their way to winning a program-record 36 victories this season, Arizona went 4-0 against teams ranked in the top-10. Michigan ended the regular season ranked third in the AP poll. 11d ago / 9:31 PM EDTMichigan's front court depth should helpThe Wolverines boast one of the biggest frontcourts in the country. Yaxel Lendeborg, the 6-foot-9 forward who's the team's leading scorer, may have picked up two quick fouls. But Michigan can still lean on Morez Johnson Jr., another 6-foot-9 forward, and Aday Mara, its 7-foot-3 center.Moments ago, Johnson ran the floor for an easy bucket in transition.11d ago / 9:31 PM EDT10-3 Wolverines at the first timeoutMichigan has the early lead in this battle of jungle cats. Four Wolverines have scored, while Jaden Bradley has Arizona’s only points so far. There’s 15:59 left in the first half. 11d ago / 9:25 PM EDTEarly disparityHow about this contrast? Michigan has already made four shots while building a 10-1 lead. Arizona only just attempted its fourth shot.11d ago / 9:25 PM EDTMichigan coming out hot!The Wolverines have opened this game on a 10-1 run only a little over two minutes in. 11d ago / 9:22 PM EDTBad news for Michigan earlyThe Wolverines’ top scorer, Yaxel Lendeborg, has picked up two fouls less than 90 seconds into the game. 11d ago / 9:21 PM EDTThe second semifinal is underway!Arizona and Michigan have tipped off! Who will face UConn in the national title game? 11d ago / 9:14 PM EDTMichigan-Arizona predictionMichigan has won by an average margin of 25 points during the tournament thanks to big runs. A pair of 8-0 runs against Alabama secured a Sweet 16 win, and one round later, the Wolverines scored 21 unanswered points to overwhelm Tennessee. They’ll pull off another to hold off a wildly talented Arizona team, 82-72.11d ago / 9:11 PM EDTArizona freshmen expected to be top NBA draft picksArizona's two leading scorers are two freshmen -- Brayden Burries and Koa Peat -- who should both be first-round picks in the NBA Draft come June.Burries, a 6-foot-4 guard, has been shooting very well in the tournament. He's averaged 17.8 points, 6.3 rebounds, and 2 assists per game in the tournament, while making 68% of his 3-pointers (13-for-19).Peat is a 6-foot-8 wing who's averaging 17.5 points per game in the tournament. He scored 20 points in Arizona's comeback win over Purdue in the Elite Eight. 11d ago / 9:02 PM EDTMichigan's Lendeborg has elevated his gameThe Wolverines are powered by Yaxel Lendeborg, the 6-foot-9 forward who transferred over last year from UAB. During the NCAA tournament, Lendeborg has elevated his game. Through the first four rounds, he's averaged 21 points while shooting 55% from 3-point range (11-for-20). If he keeps shooting like that, Arizona will have its hands full tonight. 11d ago / 8:56 PM EDTBryce James, LeBron's son, is a redshirt player for ArizonaComing out of high school, the prestigious Sierra Canyon in Southern California, Bryce James was rated as a three-star recruit, as a 6-foot-5 guard prospect. According to ESPN's recruiting website, he chose Arizona over offers from Ohio State (one of his father's favorite teams) and Duquesne.Bryce has spent this season, his first in college, as a redshirt player for the Wildcats. But the media doesn't know much about his standing on the team beyond that. 11d ago / 8:51 PM EDTKey stat for Arizona-MichiganThis is a clash of styles. By choice, Arizona attempts only 16 3-pointers per game, one of the lowest averages in the entire country. Michigan averages nine more, and has leaned on the 3 even more in the tournament, where it’s making at least 10 per game, while shooting 44%. If Michigan keeps that up, and Arizona can’t keep pace, you can do the math.11d ago / 8:46 PM EDTWildcats are led by an ArizonanTwenty-five years after Arizona last made the Final Four, it's back thanks to a super freshman from Arizona. Koa Peat, a 6-8 forward from suburban Phoenix, is averaging 14.1 points, the team's second-highest average, and 5.5 rebounds and 2.7 assists. Peat's season began with a 30-point outburst to beat defending national champion Florida in November. He hasn't scored 30 points since, and in February was held to single-digit scoring in three of four games in one stretch. In his last five games, however, Peat is averaging 18.2 points while shooting 52.4%."They call him Mr. Arizona," Wildcats coach Tommy Lloyd said. "Koa is special, and I know you guys hear it, but you got to hear it again. Four state championships at the same high school. Didn’t go to a prep school. Four gold medals with USA Basketball. No one in FIBA history has ever done that. And helped lead Arizona to a Final Four."That was my recruiting pitch. Four, four, and four. Let’s do it."11d ago / 8:40 PM EDTTommy Lloyd rebuffs North Carolina, agrees to new deal to stay at ArizonaNorth Carolina, one of the premiere programs in college basketball, needs a new head coach. One of the rumored candidates had been coach Tommy Lloyd, who's guided Arizona to its first Final Four since 2001. At a press conference this week, Lloyd was asked about the North Carolina opening. He said he was "100 percent locked in on Arizona," and that he was "excited to see what this team can do."Well, the next day, Lloyd announced he'd agreed to a new contract to stay at Arizona. He said he "didn’t want to make this entire Final Four about" his job status, and that it had been "an honor to even be considered for [the North Carolina] job," given that he'd grown up idolizing Michael Jordan."With that being said, though," he added, "I made a decision that my Michael Jordan is Steve Kerr, and I’m proud to be an Arizona Wildcat."11d ago / 8:34 PM EDTArizona primed to handle 'business’ in Final FourNumbers on the Board dives into the men's college basketball Final Four, debating which teams they believe are capable of advancing to the national championship game, with eyes on Arizona.11d ago / 8:24 PM EDTFinal: UConn 71, Illinois 62The Huskies are headed back to the national championship game for the third time in four seasons! UConn held off a late Illinois comeback to clinch its spot in the title game. 11d ago / 8:23 PM EDTThat may be it for Illinois...The Huskies lead 69-62 after Illinois' Keaton Wagler missed a 3-pointer and UConn's Jayden Ross hit a free throw on the other end. The Illini will now play the foul game. 11d ago / 8:21 PM EDTClutch free throws from UConn’s Silas Demary Jr.UConn leads 68-62 with 26.3 seconds left. 11d ago / 8:19 PM EDTBack-to-back threes!Braylon Mullins hit his first shot of the second half to give UConn a 7-point lead, but Illinois’ Keaton Wagler answered with a triple of his own to trim the deficit back to 4.Huskies lead 66-62 with 43.5 seconds to go. 11d ago / 8:16 PM EDTIllinois’ Keaton Wagler cuts the deficit to 4 pointsWagler bullied his way into the paint for a bucket, and now the Huskies’ lead is only 63-59 with 1:38 left. Each side has one timeout left. 11d ago / 8:14 PM EDTTimeout after a trap on UConn's Tarris Reed Jr.The Huskies lead 63-57 after an Illinois free throw on the previous possession.UConn is down to one timeout after Reed Jr. couldn’t work out of a double team. There's 2:08 remaining. 11d ago / 8:11 PM EDTUConn's Tarris Reed Jr. goes 2-of-2 at the free-throw lineThe Huskies lead 63-56 with under 3 minutes to go. 11d ago / 8:08 PM EDTHuge 3-pointer from Illinois' Ben Humrichous!UConn leads 61-56 with 2:46 to go.11d ago / 8:06 PM EDTFirst bucket of the second half for Tarris Reed Jr.Followed by a fastbreak dunk by Solo Ball, UConn is back up 61-53 with under 4 minutes to go. 11d ago / 8:06 PM EDTIllinois' offense finally showing lifeBrad Underwood's team has cut the deficit to just four points after being down by as many as 14 points. Despite only two assists this game, they are on a 10-2 run with five minutes left. 11d ago / 8:04 PM EDTIt’s a 4-point game!After a chaos possession and a couple offensive boards, Illinois' Andrej Stojakovic made a putback to cut the Huskies’ lead to 57-53. There's 5:01 remaining in the game.11d ago / 8:02 PM EDTUConn trying to extend a wild win streakSince 2011, UConn has won 18 consecutive games played during the second weekend or later of the NCAA tournament. It is 6-1 in its last seven appearances in the national semifinal, as well, and is 12-1 all-time in the national semifinals and finals combined. 11d ago / 8:02 PM EDTFree throws becoming huge for the IlliniIllinois has been outshot at the 3-point line, but is making up for the outside deficit by getting to the stripe. The Illini are 17-of-21 from the free-throw line, attempting 12 more freebies than the Huskies. That’s played a key role in Illinois making this a two-possession game. 11d ago / 7:59 PM EDT8-0 run for Illinois...The Illini are percolating here. An 8-0 run has made this only a 6-point game. UConn only leads 57-51 with about six minutes remaining. 11d ago / 7:57 PM EDTUConn waiting for Reed in second halfTarris Reed Jr. scored 11 points in the first half but has yet to score after halftime. In fact, he's only attempted two shots and grabbed two rebounds in this frame. The Huskies have been able to compensate, but I'm watching whether he'll have a more impactful close to the game.11d ago / 7:55 PM EDTIllinois perimeter defense a major issueThe Fighting Illinois have now allowed UConn to hit 11 3-pointers in this game, including three from Solo Ball and two from Jayden Ross. 11d ago / 7:53 PM EDTIllinois isn’t making up any groundThe Huskies lead 59-47 with 8:00 left in the game. The sides have been even in the second half, with each team scoring 20 points. But that’s not good enough for an Illinois team that desperately needs to make a push here. 11d ago / 7:44 PM EDTMeanwhile, Connecticut gets a friendly bounce off the rimIllinois must be wondering how its shots are getting an unlucky bounce while shots like this from UConn are going in.11d ago / 7:42 PM EDTHuskies holding steady in front UConn leads 52-42 with 11:49 to go.Both teams are shooting under 40% from the field, but the Huskies’ 3-point shooting has kept them comfortably in front for this entire half.The Illini will need some outside shots to drop if they’re going to mount a comeback. 11d ago / 7:41 PM EDTHow did this not go in?This non-basket has summed up Illinois' night so far.11d ago / 7:38 PM EDTUConn winning at free-throw line this halfIn the second half alone, UConn's Alex Karaban has made six free throws by himself. For the game, the Huskies are 8-for-8 at the line, while Illinois is 8-for-11.11d ago / 7:38 PM EDTIllinois continues to struggle offensivelyIllinois, considered one of the best offensive teams in the country, put up 105 against Penn in its opening-round game. But it's been a whole different story against UConn on Saturday. We're midway through the second half and so far the Fighting Illini have just two total assists. That lack of passing is a major reason why they trail by double-digits. 11d ago / 7:34 PM EDTUConn shooting just 2-for-8 in the second half The Huskies went through a shooting drought like this in the first half, as well, while making 1-of-11 shots during one stretch, and were able to still lead at halftime nonetheless. Can they get through this poor shooting stretch, too?11d ago / 7:33 PM EDTEarly in the second half, Huskies lead 47-36 UConn has outscored Illinois 10-7 to start the second half. The Huskies have a big advantage from outside, outscoring the Illini 27-12 from 3-point range. There’s 15:32 left in regulation. 11d ago / 7:29 PM EDTIllinois' David Mirković in foul troubleMirković just picked up his third foul trying to stop Alex Karaban from driving to the hoop. It's worth monitoring if the foul trouble affects his aggressiveness as he is arguably Illinois' most important player. Mirković averages 13.5 points and 8.1 rebounds per game. 11d ago / 7:22 PM EDTThe second half is underwayIllinois has never won in the NCAA Tournament when trailing by 8 or more points at half. Can the Illini make history tonight? 11d ago / 7:14 PM EDTYou’re the best player in the NCAA Tournament. It doesn’t mean you’ll have an NBA future.The award for the most outstanding player of the NCAA Tournament’s Final Four comes with prestige. Past winners form an exclusive club, including Wilt Chamberlain, Jerry West and Magic Johnson.The honor comes with a small trophy, too, one mailed to winners once March Madness concludes, an NCAA spokesperson said. What it no longer comes with, though, is job security.11d ago / 7:07 PM EDTTo reach the Final Four, Illinois needed to think outside the box. And country. Illinois head coach Brad Underwood knew something needed to change. Before this season, he had taken nine different teams to the NCAA Tournament, yet none had advanced past the Elite Eight. His teams were always championship contenders but not good enough to get over the hump.Then he made a call to Miško Ražnatović.Ražnatović, a 59-year-old Serbian, is one of the most powerful agents in basketball. He represents many of the best amateur and professional European players, including Denver Nuggets superstar Nikola Jokić, a three-time NBA MVP. Ražnatović told Underwood he had some players from the Balkans he might be interested in.Underwood didn’t want just one. He wanted them all.11d ago / 7:00 PM EDTHalftime: UConn 37, Illinois 27The Huskies finished the first half on a 16-5 run to open up an 8-point lead at halftime.UConn’s stars have shined, with Tarris Reed Jr. and Braylon Mullins combining for 23 points.Illinois’ Keaton Wagler leads his team with 10. The Fighting Illini have struggled moving the ball, though, dishing out only one assist in the half. 11d ago / 6:56 PM EDTUConn finding its offense againAfter making two field goals between the 13- and 4-minute marks of the first half, UConn has scored twice in a minute, including on this nifty transition layup from Braylon Mullins.11d ago / 6:56 PM EDTIllinois great Deron Williams in attendanceWilliams, the 3-time NBA All-Star who led Illinois to the 2005 national championship game, is in Indianapolis for today's game. 11d ago / 6:52 PM EDTWe’re getting a little back-and-forth action nowA bucket from Tarris Reed Jr. followed by a Braylon Mullins bucket plus an and-1 put UConn back ahead. Then Illinois’ Keaton Wagler and Reed traded buckets. It’s 28-24 UConn with 3:04 to go in the first. 11d ago / 6:46 PM EDTIllinois' David Mirkovic stepping up on defensive endMirkovic, a freshman from Montenegro, has come up huge on this Illinois run. He's recorded three blocks so far, including one a moment ago on UConn big man Tarris Reed Jr. 11d ago / 6:44 PM EDTUConn hasn't scored in nearly four minutesThe last time Connecticut made a field goal was with 10:16 minutes remaining in the first half, or 3:49 ago. The Huskies are down to 8-of-24 shooting from the field.11d ago / 6:42 PM EDTIllinois takes its first leadA Tomislav Ivisic 3-pointer gives the Illini a 22-21 lead, their first of the night. We're under 8 minutes to go in the first half...11d ago / 6:39 PM EDTIllinois closing in, pulls within 2 pointsThe Fighting Illini have answered UConn’s 10-2 run with a 10-3 run of their own. The score is now 21-19 Huskies with under 9 minutes to go. 11d ago / 6:35 PM EDTIllinois struggling from deepThe Fighting Illini are one of the best offensive teams in the country, with sharpshooters all over the floor, but so far that hasn't come to fruition. Coach Brad Underwood's team is 0-for-5 from 3-point range while UConn has hit three from deep already.Illinois averages 10.7 3-pointers a game, one of the top rates in college basketball. 11d ago / 6:34 PM EDTUConn's Reed a force again on the boardsAfter grabbing 40 rebounds combined in UConn's first two wins of the tournament, against Furman and UCLA, big man Tarris Reed Jr. grabbed a relatively tame 14 combined rebounds in the Huskies wins in the Sweet 16 and Elite Eight. In the early going of the Final Four, Reed Jr. looks like the version of himself from the early rounds. In nine minutes, Reed already has seven points and four rebounds.11d ago / 6:26 PM EDTUConn is on a 10-2 runThe Huskies lead 18-9 with 13:20 left in the first half. UConn's Tarris Reed Jr. and Braylon Mullins have combined for 13 points. 11d ago / 6:20 PM EDTHuskies lead at the first breakUConn has a 10-7 lead with a chance to extend it when Tarris Reed Jr. goes to free-throw line for one shot after the under-16 timeout. Outside shooting is making a difference early, as the Huskies have made two 3-pointers (on six attempts) compared to zero makes from deep for Illinois. 11d ago / 6:19 PM EDTAndrej Stojaković checks in for IllinoisStojaković, the son of legendary NBA 3-point shooter Peja, just entered the game for Illinois. He's averaging 13.6 points and 4.4 rebounds per game this season. He's coming off a 17-point outing against Iowa, during which he shot 7-for-9 from the field. 11d ago / 6:18 PM EDTUConn hero is feeling comfortable back homeUConn freshman Braylon Mullins, whose game-winning shot to beat Duke in the Elite Eight instantly made him part of March Madness lore, has already made two 3-pointers in the first four minutes. There's a reason he's comfortable — he's playing back home in his home state, where last year he was voted "Mr. Basketball" of Indiana.As his Connecticut bio notes, that award in Indiana comes with serious precedent.
